chapter: Southern Illinois roadhouse and St. Louis
title: Leaving the medicine show in Harrisburg and meeting gangster Charlie Berger
summary: The show went through Illinois to Harrisburg, where Joe jammed at the Shady Rest and gangster Charlie Berger offered him a roadhouse job.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Let me just get back to the factual side of things. Chronologically almost, we've got you to the point whereby you said you went to St. Louis. You left the medicine show in St. Louis?

No. Not at first. When I got through in St. Louis, we went up, played up through Illinois and parts of Ohio. And we wound up in Harrisburg, Illinois. We was playing in Harrisburg, which at that time was called Bloody Williamson County, where they had bunches of syndicate... They had a bunch of roadhouses in those days and bootlegging joints. We played Harrisburg, and we got off the medicine show, and they had a place called Shady Rest. The (?) said they had a good band out there, where you could go jam. They had a terrific banjo player there. They had three pieces, a drummer I can't think of... But they had a piano player who was named Eddie Miller, that made music rolls for player piano; he'd go to Chicago and make music rolls for player piano, QRS and whatever they called them... And we jammed with these guys. And this big gangster happened to come in and hear me play. There were a couple of other guys from the medicine show. His name was Charlie Berger. And he was affiliated with the Berger-Shulman Gang, which was one of the notorious bunch of racketeers in Southern Illinois -- and that's where so many guys were
killed eventually. Anyway, he asked me would I like to work in this roadhouse. He was looking for a saxophone player.
